Subject: SDK traffic choreography & retry guidance for Acme Connect

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the sandbox session this morning. Per our call, attached are: a small archive of SDK examples (sdk-samples.tar.gz) that match your Java and Go stacks, and a short runbook (redwood-sdk-runbook.pdf) focused on connectivity, timeouts, and token churn.

Quick summary of recommended defaults (we'll tune during the sandbox cutover):
- Connection and response timeouts: 3s connect, 30s read for single-request flows.
- Concurrency per host: start with 8 connections per worker, ramp to 32 based on p95 latencies.
- Retry policy: idempotent requests -> up to 4 retries; non-idempotent -> only 1 retry with request-de-dup id.
- Backoff: jittered exponential (base 200ms, factor 2, cap 3s) for transient 5xx/429.
- Token refresh: proactive refresh at T-60s; fallback to on-demand if refresh fails.

Sample client snippet (Java, okhttp):
-----------------------------------
OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(3))
  .callTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(30))
  .connectionPool(new ConnectionPool(32, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .build();

Request request = new Request.Builder().url("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate").post(body).build();

// Simple retry wrapper (pseudo)
for (int attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++) {
  Response r = client.newCall(request).execute();
  if (!shouldRetry(r)) return r;
  Thread.sleep(backoffMs(attempt));
}
-----------------------------------

Proposed next steps:
1) We schedule a 60-minute sandbox cutover (Sara from your SRE + our infra leads).
2) Run a controlled traffic replay (we can provide a script) and collect p50/p95/p99.
3) If 429s persist, we toggle token caching and reduce concurrency per worker then re-open at 10-min intervals.

I've CC'd Vanessa, Vivek, and Monica to coordinate the CSM/handoff work. If you can share a staging log sample (prefer redwood request ids if available) that will speed triage.

Attachments: sdk-samples.tar.gz, redwood-sdk-runbook.pdf

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer

Hi Alex — good questions. I dug into the staging log you attached and a few observations:

- The 429 spikes correlate with short-lived token refresh storms (multiple workers refreshing around the same time) and a sudden parallel replay wave.
- When token churn is the root cause, increasing token TTL and adding a small refresh jitter on clients is higher leverage than bluntly reducing concurrency.

Concrete fixes to try (order matters):
1) Add client-side refresh jitter: on token expiry start, jitter 0-2500ms to spread refreshes.
2) Increase token cache TTL to T+120s (while we monitor for key rotation).
3) If 429s continue: reduce per-worker concurrency from 32 -> 16 and enable per-process circuit breaker to pause new traffic for 10s when a 429 rate > 5% observed over 30s.

Backoff recommendation (detailed):
- Use jittered exponential for 429/5xx; initial = 150-300ms randomized, multiply by 2, cap at 3s; maxRetries = 4 for idempotent flows.
- Non-idempotent: include an idempotency-key header and allow 1 retry only; servers will dedupe where supported.

Small troubleshooting script we've used: log-collector.sh (attached) — run it in staging to gather host-level metrics + request traces; it zips up request ids and host CPU/queue stats.

I'll prepare a short traffic-replay manifest for your SREs so we can reproduce the pattern. Proposed sandbox cutover window: Monday 2027-06-14 09:00-10:00 PT. Can your SREs join?

Best,
Jasmine
